trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR — three items, the first MAJOR. VERIFIED CORRECT FIRST: all three algebraic clauses hold as stated over a commutative ring with involution — 1 is sigma-unitary since sigma(1)*1 = 1; closure follows from sigma(uv)uv = sigma(u)u * sigma(v)v = 1 by commutativity; rigidity is immediate (sigma(u) = u and sigma(u)u = 1 give u^2 = 1); and clause 3 is its contrapositive. The unimodularity |Phi_b(z)| = 1 for real z and real b is also correct — it is the standard consequence of the Faddeev unitarity relation. (1) FALSE IMPLICATION, and it is load-bearing. The Interpretation opens: 'On the fibre saddle — real b, so q = e^{2 pi i b^2} is a root of unity —'. Real b does NOT make q a root of unity: e^{2 pi i theta} is a root of unity if and only if theta is RATIONAL, so q is a root of unity exactly when b^2 is rational, and for generic real b it is an irrational point on the unit circle. What real b does give is |q| = 1, which is all the unimodularity argument actually needs. The error matters because 'the root-of-unity (Faddeev) saddle' is the phrase this block and its sibling rem:phi-b-bar-parity-interpretation use to separate the two archimedean faces, and the block's own evidence list is precisely the RATIONAL cases (zeta_4, zeta_5^2, zeta_6, self-dual), i.e. special b^2, not general real b. Proposed: 'real b, so |q| = 1 (and q is a root of unity exactly when b^2 is rational)'. (2) THE MANIFEST CONTRADICTS THE PROSE. The .md says the unimodularity is 'witnessed on the validated evaluator at the zeta_4, zeta_5^2, zeta_6 and self-dual points', but the .ts computation block records status: 'not_run' and carries NO witness field, while naming computations/qbeta/qbeta_fmap_phi_b_root_of_unity_reference.py (which does exist on disk, 6505 bytes). So a computational confirmation is asserted in prose that the manifest says was never run. Proposed: run the reference script and attach a witness, or downgrade 'witnessed' to 'expected'. (3) MINOR: 'analytically this is the reflection w -> -bar w of the Faddeev contour integral' is offered as the analytic ground for clause-2's hypothesis but is neither derived nor cited.
